name: input
title: Input
description: One text-entry field with a label, description and error; `type` picks text, email, url, password, search, number or tel.

when: Short free text: a name, an email, a code.
Searching or filtering a list or the app.
Entering a number: a quantity, a price, a percentage.
Any phone number a person types: sign-up, checkout, contact details.

instead.when: The text may run to several lines.

guidance.rule: Errors say what happened and what to do: "Enter a valid email: name@example.com".

builtIn: Label, description and error are announced with the input.
Required fields show "Fill in this field." after a blur or a submit; your own `errorMessage` replaces it.
The toggle is named "Show password" / "Hide password".
Formats and parses in the user's locale.
The country button is named with the country and its code.
Too short and too long say so in words.
Required fields show "Fill in this field."
youProvide: A label or placeholder that lists what can be searched.
The range in the label or description.
suggestedCountries for the markets the form expects.

keyboard.does: Increments or decrements by the step.
Opens the country list from the country button.
Searches countries by name or calling code.

genui.description: A single-line text input. Always give a label; use type email, url or tel when it fits. Emits change.

label.description: Always given; the label sits above the field, never inside it.

type.description: `text` (default), `email` or `url`: the matching keyboard and autofill on phones.

isRequired.description: Whether user input is required on the input before form submission.

appearance.description: `code` for codes, references and IDs; `numeric` for money, distance and counts.

Input.name: defaultValue
Input.description: The default value (uncontrolled).

Input.name: suppressHydrationWarning
Input.description:
A React-only flag that suppresses the warning React normally logs when an element's
server-rendered content doesn't match the client render during hydration. See [React
docs](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/client/hydrateRoot#suppressing-unavoidable-hydration-mismatch-errors).

Input.name: autoCapitalize
Input.description:
Mobile keyboards' capitalization: `none` for e-mail and codes, `characters` for codes, `words` for names.
React Aria's TextField forwards it to the input (useTextField reads it); its types leave it out, so it is declared here.

Input.name: autoFocus
Input.description: Whether the element should receive focus on render.

Input.name: enterKeyHint
Input.description:
An enumerated attribute that defines what action label or icon to preset for the enter key on
virtual keyboards. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/enterkeyhint).

Input.name: id
Input.description:
The element's unique identifier. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/id).

Input.name: slot
Input.description:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent
component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all
props received from a parent.

Input.name: spellCheck
Input.description:
An enumerated attribute that defines whether the element may be checked for spelling errors.
See [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/spellcheck).

Input.name: prefix
Input.description: Text, unit or currency before the value ("€", "https://"), or `<Icon name="search" />`.

Input.name: autoCorrect
Input.description:
An attribute that takes as its value a space-separated string that describes what, if any, type
of autocomplete functionality the input should provide. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#autocomplete).

Input.name: inputMode
Input.description:
Hints at the type of data that might be entered by the user while editing the element or its
contents. See
[MDN](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#input-modalities:-the-inputmode-attribute).

Input.name: aria-activedescendant
Input.description:
Identifies the currently active element when DOM focus is on a composite widget, textbox,
group, or application.

Input.name: aria-autocomplete
Input.description:
Indicates whether inputting text could trigger display of one or more predictions of the user's
intended value for an input and specifies how predictions would be presented if they are made.

Input.name: aria-controls
Input.description:
Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current
element.

Input.name: aria-describedby
Input.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

Input.name: aria-details
Input.description:
Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the
object.

Input.name: aria-errormessage
Input.description: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

Input.name: aria-haspopup
Input.description:
Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that
can be triggered by an element.

Input.name: aria-invalid
Input.description:
Set by a form row that owns the error text (the shared `Field` hands its control `aria-invalid`): the field
shows its invalid state as with `isInvalid`, and without an `errorMessage` of its own draws no error row,
so the row's message is the only one. It marks the input for assistive tech and draws it
invalid only: unlike `isInvalid` it never becomes the input's native validity, so it never blocks a form's
submit, and the field's own validation runs as without it.

Input.name: aria-label
Input.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

Input.name: aria-labelledby
Input.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

Input.name: onCopy
Input.description:
Handler that is called when the user copies text. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/oncopy).

Input.name: onCut
Input.description:
Handler that is called when the user cuts text. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/oncut).

Input.name: onPaste
Input.description:
Handler that is called when the user pastes text. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/onpaste).

Input.name: onCompositionEnd
Input.description:
Handler that is called when a text composition system completes or cancels the current text
composition session. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/compositionend_event).

Input.name: onCompositionStart
Input.description:
Handler that is called when a text composition system starts a new text composition session.
See [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/compositionstart_event).

Input.name: onCompositionUpdate
Input.description:
Handler that is called when a new character is received in the current text composition
session. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/compositionupdate_event).

Input.name: onFocus
Input.type: (e: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement, Element>) => void | (e: FocusEvent<Element, Element>) => void
Input.description: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.

Input.name: onBlur
Input.type: (e: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement, Element>) => void | (e: FocusEvent<Element, Element>) => void | (event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement, Element>) => void
Input.description: Handler that is called when the element loses focus.

Input.name: onChange
Input.type: (value: string) => void | (value: number) => void | (value: string, country: string) => void
Input.description: Handler that is called when the value changes.

Input.name: onBeforeInput
Input.description:
Handler that is called when the input value is about to be modified. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/beforeinput_event).

Input.name: onInput
Input.description:
Handler that is called when the input value is modified. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/input_event).

Input.name: onKeyDown
Input.description: Handler that is called when a key is pressed.

Input.name: onKeyUp
Input.description: Handler that is called when a key is released.

Input.name: onSelect
Input.description:
Handler that is called when text in the input is selected. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/select_event).

Input.name: isDisabled
Input.description: Whether the input is disabled.

Input.name: onFocusChange
Input.description: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.

Input.name: form
Input.description:
The `<form>` element to associate the input with.
The value of this attribute must be the id of a `<form>` in the same document.
See [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input#form).

Input.name: name
Input.description:
The name of the input element, used when submitting an HTML form. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#htmlattrdefname).

Input.name: value
Input.description: The current value (controlled).

Input.name: excludeFromTabOrder
Input.description:
Whether to exclude the element from the sequential tab order. If true,
the element will not be focusable via the keyboard by tabbing. This should
be avoided except in rare scenarios where an alternative means of accessing
the element or its functionality via the keyboard is available.

Input.name: render
Input.type: DOMRenderFunction<"div", TextFieldRenderProps> | DOMRenderFunction<"div", SearchFieldRenderProps> | DOMRenderFunction<"div", NumberFieldRenderProps>
Input.description:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

- You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an
  `<a>`).
- Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
- You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop
  as appropriate.

Input.name: label
Input.description: Always given; the label sits above the field, never inside it.

Input.name: errorMessage
Input.description: What happened and what to do ("Enter a valid email: name@example.com").

Input.name: isRequired
Input.description: Whether user input is required on the input before form submission.

Input.name: requiredValidation
Input.description:
Who says an empty required field is missing: `field` (default) or `app`. With `app` a DS
Form's `onSubmit` runs with the field empty, and the app's own error must clear on change. See
{@link RequiredValidation} for the whole contract.

Input.name: isOptional
Input.description: Shows "(optional)" when most of the form is required.

Input.name: isReadOnly
Input.description: Whether the input can be selected but not changed by the user.

Input.name: isInvalid
Input.description: Whether the value is invalid.

Input.name: validate
Input.type: (value: string) => true | ValidationError | null | undefined | (value: number) => true | ValidationError | null | undefined
Input.description:
A function that returns an error message if a given value is invalid.
Validation errors are displayed to the user when the form is submitted
if `validationBehavior="native"`. For realtime validation, use the `isInvalid`
prop instead.

Input.name: validationBehavior
Input.description:
Whether to use native HTML form validation to prevent form submission
when the value is missing or invalid, or mark the field as required
or invalid via ARIA.

Input.name: autoComplete
Input.description:
Describes the type of autocomplete functionality the input should provide if any. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#htmlattrdefautocomplete).

Input.name: maxLength
Input.description:
The maximum number of characters supported by the input. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#htmlattrdefmaxlength).

Input.name: min
Input.description: Bounds and step for `type="number"`; prefer NumberField for money and counts that need formatting.

Input.name: minLength
Input.description:
The minimum number of characters required by the input. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#htmlattrdefminlength).

Input.name: pattern
Input.description:
Regex pattern that the value of the input must match to be valid. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#htmlattrdefpattern).

Input.name: actions
Input.description: Extra controls at the end of the frame (`InputAction`).

Input.name: appearance
Input.description: `code` for codes, references and IDs; `numeric` for money, distance and counts.

Input.name: displayCase
Input.description:
`uppercase` shows the value in capitals (a code: "ab 123" reads "AB 123"); display only
. The input's value, `onChange` and the submitted form value stay exactly as
typed; the caret and selection follow the text as drawn. Capitals follow the page's language, as CSS
`text-transform` does (`lang="tr"`: "i" shows as "İ"), the same as `toLocaleUpperCase` in that locale. The
placeholder keeps its own case. Normalise the stored value in the app if it must be capitals.

Input.name: valueDir
Input.description:
`ltr` keeps the frame, addons and value, left to right on an RTL page: phone numbers, IBANs and
card numbers read LTR in every locale ("ME +382 67 412 908", never "908 412 67 ME +382"). The
label, help text and error still follow the page. On by default for `type` `url`, `email` and `tel`
(the placeholder then aligns LTR too); `inherit` turns that off and follows the page. Pass `ltr` for a
domain with URL addons: "https://shop.example.com", never "com. shop.example //:https".

Input.name: type
Input.description: `text` (default), `email` or `url`: the matching keyboard and autofill on phones.

Input.name: showStrength
Input.description: Four-segment meter with a word under it (create and reset only).

Input.name: isRevealed
Input.description:
Controlled visibility: `true` shows the value as text. Leave it out for the
default, where the show / hide button alone decides; set it when the app
writes a value the person should see (a "Generate" button).

Input.name: onRevealChange
Input.description: Called with the next visibility when the show / hide button is pressed.

Input.name: onSubmit
Input.description: Handler that is called when the SearchField is submitted.

Input.name: onClear
Input.description: Handler that is called when the clear button is pressed.

Input.name: shortcut
Input.description: A key hint shown at rest ("/"); the app binds the key.

Input.name: minValue
Input.description: The smallest value allowed for the input.

Input.name: maxValue
Input.description: The largest value allowed for the input.

Input.name: decrementAriaLabel
Input.description:
A custom aria-label for the decrement button. If not provided, the localized string "Decrement"
is used.

Input.name: incrementAriaLabel
Input.description:
A custom aria-label for the increment button. If not provided, the localized string "Increment"
is used.

Input.name: isWheelDisabled
Input.description: Enables or disables changing the value with scroll.

Input.name: formatOptions
Input.description:
Formatting options for the value displayed in the number field.
This also affects what characters are allowed to be typed by the user.

Input.name: commitBehavior
Input.description:
Controls the behavior of the number field when the user blurs the field after editing. 'snap'
will clamp the value to the min/max values, and snap to the nearest step value. 'validate' will
not clamp the value, and will validate that the value is within the min/max range and on a
valid step.

Input.name: showStepper
Input.description: The stepper on the end, for small integers.

Input.name: currency
Input.description:
Money: an ISO 4217 code ("EUR"). The symbol becomes a leading addon and the
amount keeps two decimals, which reads as the design's "€ 248,00" (symbol
first, with a space); Intl's own currency style has no space in tr / me.

Input.name: locale
Input.description: Formats and parses in this locale instead of the provider's (the branch locale).

Input.name: country
Input.description:
Controlled ISO country. Left out, it is read from the value, then `defaultCountry`. A shared calling
code reads back as the table's first country for it (+1 → US): pass `country` to keep Canada.

Input.name: defaultCountry
Input.description: The country an empty field opens on; by default the locale's region ("de-AT" → AT, "en" → US).

Input.name: suggestedCountries
Input.description: ISO codes shown first, above "All countries" (the markets this form expects).

Input.name: onUnsupportedInternationalPaste
Input.description: A pasted international number whose country is not offered; the value stays unchanged.

Input.name: countryLabel
Input.description:
The country button's name, from the country's name and its calling code ("Country: Germany, +49" by default, in
the provider locale). For an app that words it itself; pass it already localized.

Input.name: countryListLabel
Input.description: The country list's name ("Country" by default), also its popover's. Already localized.

Input.name: countrySearchLabel
Input.description: The country search box's name ("Search countries" by default). Already localized.

Input.name: countryEmptyMessage
Input.description: The country list's empty result for the typed search ("No results for “{query}”." by default).

Input.name: suggestedCountriesLabel
Input.description:
The name of the country list's first section, the `suggestedCountries` ("Suggested countries" by default), which assistive tech
reads as the section's name. Already localized.

Input.name: allCountriesLabel
Input.description:
The header above the rest of the list, shown when `suggestedCountries` are shown above it ("All countries" by
default). Already localized.
